decision_reason: A1 already provides a valid gravity-relative distinction among standing still, sitting and relaxing, and lying down, so no unsupported support-contact attribute is introduced for that low-U_NN pair. The main deficiencies are that knees bending (crouching) and waist bends forward differ in only smoothness despite different trunk and vertical-motion mechanics, while cycling has the weakest seen-class coverage and lacks an attribute identifying ankle-localized periodic motion. A2 therefore retains the nine supported A1 concepts and adds trunk reorientation, gravity-axis translation, and ankle-localized cyclic prominence.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or rotational motion during the activity.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: motion_regularity
attributes.definition: Temporal consistency and predictability of the motion pattern.

levels.Low: Irregular and poorly predictable motion pattern.
levels.Medium: Partly structured motion with moderate variability.

attributes.name: trunk_reorientation
attributes.definition: Extent of gravity-relative reorientation of the chest and trunk within a window, independently of motion confined to the limbs.

levels.Low: The trunk remains nearly fixed in gravity-relative orientation.
levels.Medium: The trunk undergoes moderate gravity-relative reorientation.
levels.High: The trunk undergoes large or repeated gravity-relative reorientation.

attributes.name: vertical_translation
attributes.definition: Prominence of gravity-axis linear body motion, including repeated raising or lowering, irrespective of net forward progression.

attributes.name: ankle_cyclic_prominence
attributes.definition: Degree to which periodic motion is prominently expressed at the left ankle relative to the chest and right lower arm.

levels.Low: Little or no clear ankle-localized periodic motion.
levels.Medium: Clear ankle periodicity that is not strongly dominant across body sites.
levels.High: Strong and dominant ankle-localized periodic motion.

operations.reason: Overall motion energy remains a transferable distinction between static postures, moderate articulated actions, and vigorous locomotion.
Repetition rate provides a supported contrast between fast cyclic cycling, moderate repeated locomotion or bending, and nonperiodic static postures.
Sustained rapid signal fluctuation remains distinct from impact peaks and helps transfer between smooth cyclic motion, controlled bending, and impact-rich locomotion.
Short high-magnitude changes distinguish low-impact cycling and controlled posture changes from impact-rich running and jumping.

Mean gravity-relative posture is the directly supported distinction among upright standing still, seated configurations, and nearly horizontal lying down; an additional support-contact distinction is not observable from the supplied capabilities.
Global gravity-relative configuration change separates repeated crouching from fixed standing, lying, and relatively stable cycling postures.
Overall angular-motion prominence remains useful for transferring from articulated seen activities to crouching and cycling, while remaining distinct from static orientation.
Sustained locomotor progression separates cycling and ambulatory activities from in-place postures and bending actions.
Temporal predictability is physically distinct from repetition rate and remains transferable to periodic cycling, repeated bending, and stable postures.

Chest gravity-angle change supplies a body-location-specific distinction: forward waist bending prominently reorients the trunk, whereas crouching can be dominated by lowering and lower-limb articulation with a more upright trunk. Static sitting and arm elevation provide complementary seen anchors.

Gravity-axis translation adds a directional contrast absent from general locomotor translation. It distinguishes repeated body lowering in crouching from predominantly angular waist bending and relates it to the vertical components of stair climbing and jumping.

The ankle gyro and accelerometer can support localized periodicity and cross-site coupling. This gives weakly covered cycling a transferable leg-cycle distinction from arm elevation and waist bending without duplicating cadence, because it measures where periodic motion is expressed rather than its repetition rate.

semantic_redundancy_review: The retained attributes represent distinct global concepts: energy, repetition rate, sustained fluctuation, isolated peaks, mean global posture, global posture change, angular motion, sustained locomotor translation, and temporal predictability. Trunk_reorientation is intentionally local to the chest and therefore does not duplicate global posture_variability or general rotational_motion. Vertical_translation specifies the gravity-axis component and includes repeated raising or lowering, whereas translational_motion concerns sustained progression or locomotion. Ankle_cyclic_prominence describes the body-site distribution of periodic motion, while cadence describes repetition rate and motion_regularity describes predictability. No support-contact, knee-angle, terrain, or unobserved external-device attribute is introduced.

_meta.validation: Semantic schema and complete A1-to-A2 lineage validated; no feature binding performed.
